name: Place Account Hold Request (to confirmation screen)
description: Signs on to the Meridian Core servicing console with the deployment's operator credentials, looks up a member by member number, opens the Place Account Hold action, fills in share, reason code and notes, and submits to reach the CONFIRM ACCOUNT HOLD review screen (banner: IRREVERSIBLE ACTION). It stops there without applying the hold, and returns the reviewed member, share, reason and notes for human approval. Applying the hold is supervisor-only and is refused by policy in every mode, so a teller deployment escalates to a person at that point. Returns a business outcome if no member matches the number supplied.

inputs.name: operatorId
inputs.description: Operator ID used to sign on (must have supervisor rights for the hold function).

inputs.name: memberNumber
inputs.description: Member number to place the hold on.

inputs.name: shareId
inputs.description: Share id to place the hold on, as shown in the Share ID column of the member's shares grid.

inputs.name: reasonCode
inputs.description: Hold reason code, as shown in the Reason Code dropdown.

inputs.name: notes
inputs.description: Free-text justification notes for the hold (optional; blank shows as '(none)').

outputs.name: member
outputs.description: Member number and name shown on the confirmation screen.

outputs.name: share
outputs.description: Share the hold would apply to.

outcomes.title: Hold was committed instead of stopping at review
outcomes.operatorGuidance: The capability must stop at the CONFIRM ACCOUNT HOLD screen; if a hold was actually applied, review the member's shares and the audit log immediately.

outcomes.title: Operator lacks supervisor rights for the hold function
outcomes.operatorGuidance: Open this intervention, take control of the live session, then sign on as a supervisor (super1) in that same browser and complete the hold using the details shown above. Hand control back when done. Do not re-run the capability with a different operator id: which operator this deployment acts as is bound to the deployment, not to the request.

governance.notes:
[reviewer] signon_failed: hard -> hard. A rejected sign-on is not an answer this capability was asked for - the caller wanted a balance, a transfer or a search. It means the automation cannot proceed and a human must fix the credential configuration, which is a hard failure. Only operator_sign_on, whose whole job is to sign on, reports it as a business outcome.
[reviewer] input shareId: Recorded example carried the dropdown's descriptive suffix rather than the share id a caller has.
[reviewer] checkpoint on s03: The recorded checkpoint asserted 'Signed on as S.' because this capability was discovered while signed on as a supervisor. That checks WHO signed on rather than THAT anyone did, and it made the artifact unusable by any other operator - which is the whole point of the escalation path, where a teller attempts the action and is refused. Replaced with an assertion of what the step actually guarantees.
[reviewer] supervisor_override_denied: escalate -> escalate. The recorded guidance said to re-run with a supervisor operator id. That stopped being possible when operator identity became a deployment property rather than a request parameter - and it is the first thing an on-call human reads. Replaced with what someone can actually do: take the parked session and finish it by hand.
[reviewer] description: Said 'as a supervisor operator', which is wrong and misleading in two ways: operatorId is bound to the deployment so the caller cannot choose an identity, and this deployment is a teller - which is exactly what makes the escalation structural rather than arranged. This is the tool description a routing model reads.
[reviewer] input operatorId: Example said super1, implying the caller picks the identity. operatorId is bound to the deployment via HANDSPAN_BOUND_INPUTS and is stripped from the schema the chatbot sees, so the example must show what this deployment actually acts as.
